concepts.body: Image generation takes longer than text generation; a complex request can take up to about a minute. Several settings trade quality for speed. The quality parameter offers levels such as low, medium and high; low is optimized for latency-sensitive use, so it suits quick drafts and previews, while high suits the final image. Smaller image sizes also return faster. Streaming improves how fast the app feels: set stream to true and the partial_images parameter (1 to 3), and the API sends partial images while the final one is being made, so users see progress early. Simpler prompts help when requests time out. For example, a design tool could generate four low-quality options quickly, let the user pick one, then regenerate that idea at high quality. Remember that streaming improves perceived speed only, while lower quality or smaller sizes reduce the actual work. On the exam, 'fast drafts first, best image last' means low quality for drafts and high quality for the final version.

concepts.heading: Editing Images with a Prompt and a Mask
concepts.body: You don't always need a brand-new image. The Image Edit API changes an existing image based on a text prompt, and it is generally available. You send the input image (PNG or JPG) and a prompt such as 'Add a beach ball in the center'. To limit the change to one area, add a mask: a PNG file with the same dimensions as the input image, where fully transparent pixels mark the area to edit. Filling in a masked area this way is called inpainting. The input_fidelity parameter controls how closely the result keeps the style and features of the input, such as faces, so subtle edits leave unrelated areas alone; gpt-image-1-mini doesn't support it. For example, a furniture shop that wants to replace only the sofa in a room photo uses the edit endpoint with a mask over the sofa, instead of generating a whole new room. The images playground supports the same inpainting without code. On the exam, 'change one part, keep the rest' is editing with a mask.

concepts.heading: Safety Filters and Saving the Output
concepts.body: Image generation in Foundry applies input and output moderation to all image models, as well as content filtering and abuse monitoring. If the prompt is flagged, no image is made and the error code is contentFilter. If the prompt passes but the generated image is flagged, the message reads 'Generated image was filtered as a result of our safety system', which tells you the output check, not the prompt check, blocked it. Photorealistic images of minors are blocked by default, and opting out of content filtering requires an approved request. The output format is also worth knowing: models such as GPT-image-2 and the GPT-image-1 family return images only as base64 text in the b64_json field, with no URL option. Your code decodes the base64 string into bytes and writes them to a file such as poster.png. For example, a script that prints a long block of letters instead of showing a picture simply hasn't decoded the b64_json value yet.

examPoints: A question that proposes dall-e-3 for a new image app is testing its retirement; choose a GPT-image model, with GPT-image-2 generally available and the GPT-image-1 family in limited access preview.
A question about changing only part of an existing picture is testing the Image Edit API with a mask (inpainting), not generating a new image.

A question about a blocked result is testing moderation: contentFilter for a flagged prompt, 'Generated image was filtered' for a flagged output; one about saving results is testing base64 b64_json output.

quiz.q: A developer's script calls a GPT-image model and prints a very long string of letters and numbers instead of producing a picture. What should the script do?
choices: Request the image as a URL instead, since GPT-image models return links to hosted files
Decode the base64 b64_json value into bytes and write those bytes to an image file
Raise the quality setting to high, because low-quality images are returned as plain text
Send the string to a vision-enabled chat model, which converts the text back into an image
quiz.explain: Models such as GPT-image-2 return images only as base64 in b64_json, so the script must decode and save them. Choice A is tempting because some image APIs offer URLs, but these models have no URL output option.

quiz.q: A team wants to replace only the sky in a landscape photo with a sunset and keep everything else unchanged. Which approach fits best?
choices: Use the Image Edit API with the photo, a prompt, and a mask whose transparent area covers the sky
Generate a new image from a detailed text prompt that describes the landscape and the new sunset
Send the photo to a vision-enabled chat model and ask it to describe the landscape with a sunset
Deploy dall-e-3 and use its variations feature to create versions of the photo with new skies
quiz.explain: Editing with a mask changes only the transparent area and keeps the rest of the photo. Choice B is tempting because the prompt can describe the same scene, but a newly generated image won't keep the original landscape unchanged.

days.recap: GPT-image models in Foundry create images from prompts that describe content and style, trade quality for speed, edit existing images with a mask, are tested in the images playground with View code, pass input and output moderation, and return base64 data that your code decodes and saves, while dall-e-3 is retired.

days.title: Information Extraction with Content Understanding
services: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools

concepts.heading: Content Understanding and Analyzers
concepts.body: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools uses generative AI to turn documents, images, audio and video into structured output, either Markdown for search and RAG or JSON that matches a schema you define. It is part of the Foundry resource; API version 2025-11-01 is generally available for production. The central object is the analyzer, which sets how content is processed: content extraction settings, the field schema, and the model deployments to use. Prebuilt analyzers come in three groups: base analyzers for each content type (prebuilt-document, prebuilt-image, prebuilt-audio, prebuilt-video), RAG analyzers such as prebuilt-documentSearch, and domain-specific analyzers such as prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-receipt, prebuilt-idDocument and prebuilt-contract. A custom analyzer derives from one of the four base analyzers and adds your own fields. For example, start with prebuilt-invoice for invoices, and build a custom analyzer only for fields it lacks.

concepts.heading: Field Methods: Extract, Generate, and Classify
concepts.body: Each field in an analyzer schema has a name, a type, a plain-language description and a method. Extract copies a value exactly as it appears in the content, such as an invoice number or a date on a receipt, and works for documents only. Generate produces a value the model infers or writes, such as a summary of a call, a risk level, or a description of a video scene. Classify picks one value from a predefined list, such as document type, call sentiment or chart type. If you don't set a method, the service chooses one from the type and description, but setting it explicitly gives more predictable results. Repeating rows, such as invoice line items, become an array of objects with typed properties. Clear, affirmative descriptions that list aliases ('the total due, also called amount payable') improve results before you add labeled examples. For example, a contract analyzer could extract the start date, generate a one-line summary and classify the contract type.

concepts.heading: Confidence Scores and Grounding
concepts.body: Content Understanding returns more than values. For document analyzers, the estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence setting adds a confidence score from 0 to 1 for each field and grounding, the page and bounding region where the value came from, plus text spans. Extract fields always need it turned on. These two outputs make straight-through processing possible: values with high confidence flow into automation, and only doubtful ones go to a person, who can use grounding to jump to the exact spot in the original file. Learn recommends stricter thresholds for critical fields, such as payment amounts, and tuning thresholds on your own documents. One limit matters: today only document analyzers return confidence scores, so for image, audio and video fields you design other checks. For example, an accounts team might auto-approve invoice totals above a confidence threshold and send the rest to review, with the bounding box highlighting the total on the scanned page.

concepts.heading: Documents, Images, Audio, and Video
concepts.body: One service covers all four content types. For documents, content extraction performs OCR and layout analysis, and prebuilt-read or prebuilt-layout give text and structure only, without a language model, so they cost less. prebuilt-documentSearch prepares documents for RAG, describing figures and returning Markdown. For images, prebuilt-imageSearch makes pictures searchable by description, and a custom analyzer derived from prebuilt-image uses generate or classify fields, since extract is for documents only. For audio, analyzers return a speaker-separated, time-stamped transcript; prebuilt-audioSearch adds a summary, and prebuilt-callCenter returns call-center insights. For video, prebuilt-videoSearch returns segmented Markdown with descriptions, transcripts and key frames, and segmentation can split a video by a rule you describe. Analyzers that generate fields need deployed Foundry models set as the resource's defaults. For example, a podcast library could call prebuilt-audioSearch to get transcripts and summaries without defining any fields.

concepts.heading: Calling an Analyzer and Choosing the Right Tool
concepts.body: Analysis is asynchronous. With REST you POST the file to `/contentunderstanding/analyzers/{analyzerId}:analyze`; the service answers 202 Accepted with an Operation-Location header, and you poll that URL until status is Succeeded, then read the result's contents and fields. The SDK wraps the same pattern in a poller whose result you wait for. A client needs the resource endpoint, a credential (a key or Microsoft Entra ID) and the analyzer ID. When to use what: Content Understanding analyzers fit unstructured or varied documents, multimodal content, inferred fields and zero-shot extraction without labeling. Azure Document Intelligence fits structured forms with common templates, custom models trained on labeled samples, and on-premises containers. A plain multimodal model with your own prompts gives full control, but you must build OCR, schemas, confidence scores and grounding yourself. For example, a package mixing a PDF, photos and a voice note suits Content Understanding.

examPoints: A question that asks how a field gets its value is testing field methods: extract for printed values in documents, generate for inferred values or summaries, classify for one option from a list.
A question about routing only doubtful values to people, or showing where a value came from, is testing confidence scores and grounding, which document analyzers return.

A question that compares Content Understanding, Document Intelligence and a prompt-only model is testing their fit: multimodal and zero-shot, structured forms and containers, or full control with everything built yourself.

quiz.q: A team defines a custom document analyzer for insurance claims. It needs the claim number exactly as printed, a short summary of the incident, and the claim type from a fixed list of five. Which field methods fit?
choices: Generate for all three fields, because a language model writes every value in the result
Classify for the claim number and summary, and extract for the claim type from the list
Extract for the claim number, generate for the summary, and classify for the claim type
Extract for all three fields, because each value comes from the same claim document
quiz.explain: Extract copies printed values, generate writes inferred text such as a summary, and classify picks from a fixed list. Choice D is tempting because all values relate to the document, but the summary doesn't appear in it and the type must come from the list.

quiz.q: A developer posts a file to a Content Understanding analyzer with the REST API and receives 202 Accepted, but the response body has no extracted fields. What should the code do next?
choices: Send the same file again to the :analyze endpoint until the response returns 200 OK
Switch to a prebuilt-read analyzer, which returns all fields in the first response
Create a custom analyzer, because prebuilt analyzers always return an empty response
Poll the Operation-Location URL until the status is Succeeded, then read the result
quiz.explain: Analysis is asynchronous: 202 hands back an Operation-Location to poll until the status is Succeeded. Choice A is tempting because the request looks unfinished, but resending only starts new analysis operations.

days.recap: Azure Content Understanding analyzers, prebuilt or custom, turn documents, images, audio and video into Markdown or schema fields using extract, generate and classify methods, return confidence and grounding for documents, run through an analyze-then-poll pattern, and suit multimodal, zero-shot work where Document Intelligence suits structured forms.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: AI-901 is a Fundamentals exam, and Learn's exam duration page gives Fundamentals exams 45 minutes to answer, inside a longer seat time for instructions and the candidate agreement. You pass with a scaled score of 700 or greater. Microsoft does not publish the number of questions for AI-901, so pace yourself by time rather than by a fixed count. The two domains are Identify AI concepts and capabilities at 40 to 45 percent and Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry at 55 to 60 percent, so the hands-on Foundry domain carries more weight. Microsoft does not list the question types in advance; the exam sandbox lets you try the interface beforehand. Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but the exam may include preview features if they are commonly used, and the study guide expects familiarity with REST APIs, SDKs and CLIs, so read short code snippets calmly.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: AI Concepts and Workloads
concepts.body: Many wrong answers come from look-alike pairs. Transparency explains a decision or discloses that AI is involved, while accountability keeps a named person answerable and in control. Fairness is about different outcomes for similar groups, while reliability and safety is about failures in unusual conditions. RAG adds changing or private knowledge with citations, while fine-tuning changes behavior, tone or format. Training changes weights, while every chat request is inference with fixed weights. Temperature and top_p shape randomness, max tokens caps length, and a stop sequence ends output at a marker. Generative AI writes or answers, while agentic AI also uses tools to act. Sentiment analysis gives one label per sentence or document, while opinion mining links opinions to targets. Extractive summaries quote, abstractive ones reword. OCR returns text, while Content Understanding returns named fields. Captioning is image in, text out, while image generation is text in, image out.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Building with Foundry
concepts.body: The second domain has its own traps. The system message holds fixed role, scope, format and fallback rules, while the user message holds what changes on each call. In code, the model parameter takes your deployment name, not the catalog name of the model. A plain model call has no saved instructions or tools, while an agent in Foundry Agent Service is a saved, versioned combination of model, instructions and tools; a conversation holds the history and a response is one run. Classic threads, messages and runs are deprecated in favor of conversations and responses. Azure Language gives fixed, repeatable output such as PII redaction, while a prompted model gives flexible, combined answers. A speech pipeline gives control over voices and SSML, while a speech-in, speech-out model answers spoken prompts directly. Vision-enabled chat models turn images into text, while GPT-image models turn text into images. Prebuilt analyzers come first; build a custom analyzer only for missing fields.

concepts.heading: Use an Error Log
concepts.body: For every practice question you miss or guess, write down the pair of ideas you confused, such as RAG versus fine-tuning or object detection versus segmentation, and the clue in the stem that should have decided it. Reviewing these pairs is faster than rereading every day, because the same confusions tend to repeat. Give the most time to the Foundry implementation domain, the larger one, unless your log shows a clear weak spot elsewhere. Read each scenario for its deciding phrase, such as must stay in the EU, overnight, word for word, takes action, or who said what, before looking at the choices, and eliminate choices that solve a different problem. Also watch for old names and retired features in distractors: Azure AI Foundry is now Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI services are now Foundry Tools, content filters are now guardrails, DALL-E 3 is retired, and Image Analysis is deprecated with retirement set for 2028.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Plan
concepts.body: For an online exam, check your room, webcam and system well before the start time; for a test center, arrive early. Read the overview pages at the start, because they explain the item types and whether you can return to questions. Make a first pass answering what you know and mark uncertain questions for review where that is allowed. You may take unscheduled breaks, but the exam clock keeps running, and after a break you cannot return to questions you already viewed, so finish and review a section before stepping away. With 45 minutes and an unpublished question count, check the timer now and then rather than spending long on one item. For multi-answer questions, choose exactly the number requested. Microsoft states there is no penalty for guessing, because a wrong answer simply earns no points, and some questions may be unscored, so answer every question as if it counts.

examPoints: A question that lists RAG, fine-tuning and a larger context window as choices is testing whether you can tell adding changing knowledge apart from changing behavior and simply allowing longer prompts.

A question that lists Azure Language, a prompted generative model and Content Understanding as choices is testing whether the need is a fixed text analysis result, a flexible combined answer, or named fields extracted from documents and media.

A question that describes a solution reading data and acting through tools, or that asks where an agent's history lives, is testing agentic AI and Foundry Agent Service (agents, conversations and responses) rather than a plain chat call.

quiz.q: A learner keeps confusing two ways of adding company information to a chat assistant. Which statement correctly separates RAG from fine-tuning?
choices: RAG retrains the model's weights on company files, while fine-tuning searches an index at question time
RAG and fine-tuning both need a provisioned deployment type, and neither one can be used with Global Standard
RAG retrieves current passages at question time, while fine-tuning teaches behavior or style from examples
RAG changes the tone and output format of answers, while fine-tuning adds facts that change every week
quiz.explain: RAG grounds each answer in passages retrieved when the question arrives, while fine-tuning adjusts a model's behavior from many examples. Choice A is tempting because it names both real mechanisms, but it swaps them between the two approaches.

quiz.q: A team wants each user's chat with its Foundry agent to keep its own history across several turns. What should the client app do?
choices: Create one conversation per chat session and pass its ID with each response it requests
Create a new agent version for every user so that each version stores only that user's history
Add the full chat history to the agent's instructions before each user message is sent in
Raise the max tokens setting on the model deployment so that the agent remembers older turns
quiz.explain: In Foundry Agent Service a conversation holds the history, so one conversation per session keeps turns together and separate from other users. Choice B is tempting because agents are versioned, but a version is the agent's definition (model, instructions and tools), not a store for one user's chat history.

days.recap: AI-901 gives 45 minutes with a scaled pass mark of 700 and an unpublished question count, weighted toward building with Microsoft Foundry; drill the confused pairs, read each scenario for its deciding clue, prefer current GA names and features, and answer every item before submitting.
